statement.p: By your cell phone contract, you pay a monthly fee plus {\$0.05} for each minute you spend on the phone. In one month, you spent 220 minutes over the phone, and had a bill totaling {\$27.00}.

Let x be the number of minutes you spend on the phone in a month, and let y be your total cell phone bill for that month, in dollars. Use a linear equation to model your monthly bill based on the number of minutes you spend on the phone.
This lines slope-intercept equation is .
If you spend 180 minutes on the phone in a month, you would be billed .
If your bill was {\$40.50} one month, you must have spent minutes on the phone in that month.

li.p: A lines equation in slope-intercept form looks like y=mx+b, where m is the slope, and y is the y-coordinate of the y-intercept. The slope of the linear model has been given to us: {\$0.05} per minute.
So now we have that y=0.05x+b. The next step is to find the value of b. There are at least two ways.
One way is to substitute a given point into y={0.05x}+b. We have the point (220,27).

p.m: \begin{aligned} y \amp = {0.05x} + b \\ 27 \amp = 0.05 \cdot 220 + b \\ 27 \amp = 11 + b \\ 27\mathbf{{}-11} \amp = 11 + b\mathbf{{}-11} \\ 16 \amp = b\\ b \amp = 16 \end{aligned}

li.p: This lines slope-intercept equation is y={0.05x}+16.
Another way is to use the lines point-slope equation y-y_{1}=m(x-x_{1}). Again, we use the point (220,27).
This is the second way to find b, and thus the lines slope-intercept equation is y=0.05x+16.
In one month, you spent 180 minutes on the phone. To find out the bill, we substitute 180 in for x in the equation y=0.05x+16, and we have:
If you spent 180 minutes over the phone in a month, your bill for that month would be {\$25.00}.
In one month, you had a cell phone bill of {\$40.50}. To find how many minutes you spent on the phone that month, we substitute 40.5 in for y in the equation y=0.05x+16, and we have:
If your bill was {\$40.50} in one month, you must have spent 490 minutes on the phone.
